title: Short Stuff: Magic 8 Ball
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Magic 8 Ball toy. Covers its origins in a prototype made by Albert Carter, inspired by his clairvoyant mother in Cincinnati, the early Psychoseer and Pocket Fortune Teller versions, and the partnership with brother-in-law Abe Bookman, who founded A. Labe Crafts after Carter's death. Brunswick Billiard Company prompted the billiard-ball eight-ball design, and the toy was first sold as a paperweight before teens made it a hit. The hosts describe the 20-sided die with 10 affirmative, 5 negative and 5 non-committal answers, and explain the term "MacGuffin" with a Simpsons example. The episode closes with a brief tangent on pronunciation feedback and an ad read.
topics: The Simpsons Bart Millhouse Magic 8 Ball episode

segments.title: Welcome and introduction to the Magic 8 Ball
segments.summary: Josh introduces the Short Stuff episode on the Magic 8 Ball. Chuck describes the toy's look and how it is used.

segments.title: Origins: Albert Carter, his mother's psychic writing device, and Abe Bookman
segments.summary: Carter, inspired by his clairvoyant mother in Cincinnati, built a prototype during World War Two called the Psycho-Seer. Brother-in-law Abe Bookman helped form the partnership. The device was patented as the Psychoseer, later renamed the Pocket Fortune Teller. In 1946 they formed A. Lablabe Crafts, and Carter died, leaving Bookman as sole owner.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: The hosts take a break before returning to the story.

segments.title: Brunswick and the billiard eight ball design
segments.summary: Brunswick Billiard Company of Chicago took interest in the Psychoseer in 1950 and asked Bookman to make an eight-ball version. Bookman built a plastic eight ball around the device with a single die. The 20-sided die has 10 affirmative, 5 negative, and 5 non-committal answers. The hosts note the toy is mostly used for playful questions like whether a crush likes you.

segments.title: Early marketing as a paperweight and the rise among teens
segments.summary: Bookman first sold the toy as an adult novelty paperweight, which was a poor business move. Teens then bought it and it became a hit, selling about a million a year. The hosts compare it to New Coke as a product that missed what people wanted.

segments.title: MacGuffin explained
segments.summary: Josh asks Chuck to explain the term MacGuffin, since the Magic 8 Ball is often used as one in film and TV. Chuck describes it as an object of low real importance that has high importance in driving the plot, using a treasure map example. Josh contrasts it with a boondoggle.

segments.title: Magic 8 Ball in The Simpsons and Romancing the Stone
segments.summary: Josh cites a 1992 Simpsons episode in which Bart and Millhouse consult the Magic 8 Ball about their friendship, and it predicts the friendship will end that day. Bart later strikes Millhouse with the toy after a fight over a new girl. The hosts also mention Romancing the Stone.

segments.title: Pronunciation feedback and tangent
segments.summary: The hosts discuss listener feedback about not checking pronunciations, including the chip maker Nvidia, and a confusion with a skincare brand.

segments.title: Sign-off and iHeartRadio network promo
segments.summary: Closing credits and a promo for the iHeartRadio app and podcasts.
